covers.quote: hide information in the alt text, as a user might not see it

rules.quote: Don’t write something in the alt text that a user can’t learn from seeing the image or reading the caption or title.
rules.violation_condition: Alt text contains information unavailable to someone viewing the image and reading its caption or title.
rules.why: G-4: the later sentence states the earlier list prohibition in directly actionable wording.

covers.quote: Don’t repeat the information provided by the image and alt text.

rules.quote: repeat information in the alt text that a user would read in the caption
rules.violation_condition: An image’s alt text duplicates information in its caption, causing the same information to be read twice.
when: Read the quoted list item under its lead-in, ‘Don’t:’.
A caption that fully describes an image can support empty alt text rather than a duplicate description.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: repeated descriptions across the image’s text alternatives are one duplication check.

covers.quote: use the <longdesc> attribute for extended descriptions.

rules.quote: Do not use the <longdesc> attribute.
rules.violation_condition: An extended description is supplied through a <longdesc> attribute.
rules.why: G-4: the two prohibitions are the same check; the later sentence is self-contained.

covers.quote: Add alternative text for all images.
Include alt text and captions for all informative photographs and illustrations.

rules.quote: Add alt text to all images
rules.violation_condition: An image has no alt-text provision, including no explicit empty alternative or decorative designation where appropriate.
when: Decorative images require an explicit empty alternative or the document’s decorative-image designation, not a descriptive alternative.
Informative images can have empty alt text in the stated cases where surrounding text fully supplies their information.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: image categories change the acceptable alternative, not the requirement to provide one.

rules.quote: Include short alt text – less than about 100 characters – for all informative images.
rules.specification: Interpret ‘less than about 100 characters’ as fewer than 100 characters: flag 100 or more. Count the decoded alt-text value, including spaces and punctuation, not the surrounding markup. This exact boundary is an implementation choice.
rules.violation_condition: An informative image’s alt text reaches or exceeds the operational character limit.
when: Applies to descriptive alt text for informative images.
rules.why: G-1 and E-4: brevity is distinct from alt-text presence, and the approximate limit needs an explicit interpretation.

covers.quote: Write alt text that conveys the same important information as the image.
Describe the informational icon so the user can understand what it is.
State the functional icon’s purpose so the user can understand the outcome.
alt text that contains a brief interpretation of the main idea from the image
If the caption or nearby text already explains the informational image, you might use very brief alt text.
Examples of informative images that might have an empty value in the alt text include:
a photograph with a caption that is a full description of the content and function of the photograph
a snapshot of a software screen that the text describes
an illustration of an idea that the text describes.

examples.note: The example describes the informational icon.

parts.quote: An informational printer icon: alt="Printer icon"

examples.note: The example states the functional icon’s outcome.

parts.quote: A functional printer icon: alt="Print this page"

examples.note: Read both blocks together: nearby instructions permit very brief alt text.

parts.quote: You might use alt="Screenshot of dropdown menu and buttons" if the nearby
text (for example, the caption) had this instruction:Select the ‘save’ button between the ‘Tools’ drop-down and the ‘Cancel’ button

rules.quote: Write alternative text that describes the information or function of the image.
rules.violation_condition: Provided alt text fails to convey the image’s important information or intended function.
when: For informative images, convey the same important information as the image.
For informational icons, describe the icon so the user can understand what it is.
For functional icons, state the purpose or outcome.
For complex images, give a brief interpretation of the main idea in alt text; put fuller details in an extended description.
Alt text can be very brief when the caption or nearby text already explains the image.
An informative image can have empty alt text when a full caption or surrounding text already describes its content and function.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: information, function and image complexity change what the same descriptive-adequacy check expects.

covers.quote: Add captions for all images, unless they are only decorative.
Include alt text and captions for all informative photographs and illustrations.

rules.quote: Include captions for all images that are not decorative
rules.violation_condition: A non-decorative image has no caption.
when: Decorative images are exempt.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the decorative exception and the photograph restatement belong to one caption-presence check.

covers.quote: Use captions to acknowledge the creator or copyright holder of images in captions.

rules.quote: When referencing, you must attribute copyright material.
rules.violation_condition: Referenced copyright material has no attribution.
when: Applies to copyright images and text.
rules.why: G-4: the copyright requirement supplies the explicit mandatory force for attribution.

covers.quote: Use captions to acknowledge the creator or copyright holder of images in captions.

rules.quote: Write the attribution as part of the caption or following the copyright material.
rules.violation_condition: An attribution is present but is neither in the caption nor following the copyright material.
when: Applies where attribution is required.
Either placement stated by the manual is acceptable.
rules.why: G-2: caption placement and placement following the material are alternatives within one location check.

rules.quote: Use your organisation’s referencing style.
rules.specification: The organisation’s referencing style must be supplied before compliance can be determined.
rules.violation_condition: An image reference or attribution does not follow the organisation’s prescribed referencing style.
when: Applies to image references and attributions in this section.
rules.why: G-5: unlike an instruction to consult a source, this specifies an observable property of references.

examples.note: The four blocks form one HTML example.

parts.quote: <figure>
<figcaption>Figure 3: Kangaroo numbers in Victoria from 1880 to 1980</figcaption>
...

rules.quote: Include the HTML <figcaption> element to associate the caption with the image.
rules.violation_condition: An HTML image caption is not associated with its image using a <figcaption> element.
when: Applies to image captions in HTML.
rules.why: The required semantic markup is a checkable property of the caption, not visual layout.

covers.quote: Decorative images should have null alt text (alt="").
This is 2 double quotation marks with no space (alt="").
An image is decorative if you can remove it from the page without losing any meaning or information.
Use empty alt text (alt="") to declare it as decorative.

examples.note: The decorative icon has an empty alternative.

parts.quote: A decorative printer icon: alt=""

rules.quote: Include an empty value, or null text, for alt text if the image is decorative.
rules.violation_condition: A decorative image has a non-empty alt-text value.
when: An image is decorative if removing it loses no meaning or information.
An HTML empty value is alt="", with no space between the quotation marks.
Includes decorative icons.
For document formats with a decorative-image setting, the page instead directs authors to use that setting.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: decorative icons are a case of the same empty-value rule; missing alt text is checked separately.

rules.quote: Include keywords in the surrounding text to support search engines.
rules.specification: The page does not identify which keywords are required or how much surrounding text to examine.
rules.violation_condition: The text surrounding an image lacks the relevant keywords needed to make its information discoverable.
when: The instruction appears in the decorative-images discussion, where keywords must not be supplied through descriptive alt text.
rules.why: This specifies surrounding wording, but its keyword and context boundaries need clarification.

rules.quote: Don’t create alt text to add keywords.
rules.violation_condition: Alt text is created for keyword insertion rather than to provide an appropriate text alternative.
when: In particular, do not replace decorative images’ empty alternatives with keywords.
Relevant words occurring naturally in a useful description are not prohibited.
rules.why: The prohibited use of alt text is distinct from the requirement for keywords in surrounding text.

covers.quote: a caption that summarises the image

rules.quote: Add captions and titles that give context.
rules.specification: Assess whether the caption or title explains the image’s relevance in its surrounding content. For complex images, the page specifies that the caption summarises the image. Do not treat this as a separate requirement to title every image.
rules.violation_condition: An informational image’s caption or title fails to provide context for the image.
when: Applies to informational images.
For complex images, the caption should summarise the image.
rules.why: G-2: the complex-image summary is a specific case of a contextual caption, not another caption-presence rule.

covers.quote: For logos that are functional links to home pages, use the name of the site in the link instead of the alt text.

rules.quote: Write the full name of the organisation in the logo alt text.
rules.violation_condition: A non-home-page-link logo’s alt text omits or abbreviates the organisation’s full name.
when: Logos functioning as links to home pages follow the separate site-name-in-link instruction.
rules.why: G-2: the functional-logo case limits the full-organisation-name requirement.

covers.quote: You don’t need to add the name to the link if it is already in the text on the page.

rules.quote: For logos that are functional links to home pages, use the name of the site in the link instead of the alt text.
rules.specification: The page distinguishes the site name ‘in the link’ from the logo’s alt text but does not specify the required HTML implementation or whether other accessible-name mechanisms qualify.
rules.violation_condition: A logo linking to a home page supplies the site name only in alt text instead of in the link, or omits the required site name from the link when it is not already on the page.
when: Applies only to logos that link to home pages.
The site name need not be added to the link if it is already in the text on the page.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the existing page text is an exception to the link-name requirement, not an independent permission rule.

covers.quote: Use the extended description to help the user understand the information in the image.
Complex images contain too much information to include in the alt text alone.

examples.note: The page presents this as an extended-description example.

parts.quote: Users are at the centre of the content lifecycle. The cycle starts with intent. It then moves through 6 stages: discover needs; draft; test; approve; publish; maintain. The process is circular. The cycle shows continuous improvement through repetition. Stages can repeat before completing a full cycle.

rules.quote: an extended description with more details about the data in the image, usually referencing the title or caption of the image.
rules.violation_condition: A complex image lacks an extended description giving fuller details of its data.
when: Read the quoted item under the instruction to include information for complex images.
Applies to images with too much information for alt text alone.
Referencing the image title or caption is usual, not an unconditional requirement.
rules.why: G-1 and G-4: this is the extended-description child requirement, distinct from alt text and captions.

rules.quote: Link in-text references to the image title only if it helps the user.
rules.specification: The page does not define what benefit makes such a link helpful; a usefulness criterion is needed.
rules.violation_condition: An in-text reference is linked to an image title without providing a useful benefit to the user.
when: Applies to links from in-text references to image titles.
rules.why: G-3: ‘only if’ restricts links and can produce a finding; it is not merely permission to link.

rules.quote: Write the extended description on the same page or, if it is very long, link to it on a separate page.
rules.specification: The page does not define ‘very long’; no numerical cutoff is assumed.
rules.violation_condition: An extended description is off-page without a link, or is off-page despite not qualifying as very long.
when: The default location is the same page.
A very long extended description may instead be linked on a separate page.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the separate-page option is an exception within one location-and-access check.

rules.quote: Put most of the interpretation of the image in the body text.
rules.specification: The page does not specify how to measure the share of interpretation; word count is not assumed to be an adequate measure.
rules.violation_condition: Most interpretation of an image is placed outside the body text, such as in its extended description.
when: Appears in the guidance for complex images and extended descriptions.
rules.why: This checks the distribution of interpretation, not the presence or location of the extended description itself.

covers.quote: use an initial capital for title text that comes after the colon.

rules.quote: Capitalise the first word and proper nouns only.
rules.violation_condition: A title or caption has an uncapitalised first word or proper noun, or capitalises other words as title case.
when: Applies to image titles and captions.
